Define interfaces for object creation, letting subclasses decide which concrete classes to instantiate.

💡 Key Concepts

  • Factory Method: Abstracts instantiation of a single product family using subclasses.
  • Abstract Factory: Interface to create families of related products without specifying concrete classes.
  • Loose Coupling: Keeps callers decoupled from specific constructor implementations.

💻 Practical Code Example

C# / CODE BLOCK
public interface IButton { void Render(); }
public abstract class UIControlFactory {
    public abstract IButton CreateButton();
}

⚠️ Common Pitfalls & Mistakes

Adding too many product variants, which requires editing and complicating the factory classes.

questions.question: What is the difference between Factory Method and Abstract Factory?
questions.answer: Factory Method uses inheritance to instantiate a single product. Abstract Factory uses composition to create families of related products.

questions.question: How does the Factory pattern follow the Open/Closed principle?
questions.answer: You can introduce new product implementations without changing the client code that consumes the factory.

topics.title: Builder Pattern
topics.html:
Builder Pattern

Course: Design Patterns

Construct complex objects step-by-step using fluent method interfaces.

💡 Key Concepts

  • Step-by-step Construction: Adding configurations to an object incrementally.
  • Fluent Interface: Methods return "this" to allow method chaining.
  • Build Method: A final method that returns the fully configured object.

💻 Practical Code Example

C# / CODE BLOCK
var doc = new DocumentBuilder()
    .AddTitle("Report")
    .AddAuthor("Ashutosh")
    .Build();

⚠️ Common Pitfalls & Mistakes

Using the Builder pattern for simple objects that could be initialized easily using standard properties.

questions.question: When is the Builder pattern useful?
questions.answer: When an object requires complex, multi-step configuration or has constructor parameter configurations.

questions.question: What is a fluent API in the Builder pattern?
questions.answer: A syntax design where builder methods return the builder instance (this), allowing method chaining.

topics.title: Prototype Pattern
topics.html:
Prototype Pattern

Course: Design Patterns

Clone existing objects to create new instances, avoiding expensive creation steps.

💡 Key Concepts

  • Cloning: Copying an existing object instance.
  • Shallow vs Deep Copy: Shallow copies copy references. Deep copies recursively copy referenced objects.
  • ICloneable: Standard .NET interface used to implement object cloning.

💻 Practical Code Example

C# / CODE BLOCK
public class User : ICloneable {
    public string Name { get; set; }
    public object Clone() => this.MemberwiseClone(); // Shallow copy
}

⚠️ Common Pitfalls & Mistakes

Relying on MemberwiseClone() (shallow copy) when your object has reference fields, which shares objects between clones.

questions.question: What is the difference between a shallow copy and a deep copy?
questions.answer: A shallow copy copies value properties and references. A deep copy creates new instances of all nested reference properties.

questions.question: When should you use the Prototype pattern?
questions.answer: When creating a new object is computationally expensive or requires external resources (like database lookups).

topics.title: Adapter Pattern
topics.html:
Adapter Pattern

Course: Design Patterns

Convert the interface of a class into another interface that clients expect, enabling incompatible systems to work together.

💡 Key Concepts

  • Wrapper: Converts requests from a target interface to a client interface.
  • Target / Adaptee: Target is the interface expected by clients. Adaptee is the incompatible class being adapted.
  • Loose Coupling: Enables legacy code integration without changing source structures.

💻 Practical Code Example

C# / CODE BLOCK
public class LegacyPrinter { public void PrintLegacy(string s) { } }
public interface IPrinter { void Print(string s); }
public class PrinterAdapter : IPrinter {
    private LegacyPrinter legacy = new LegacyPrinter();
    public void Print(string s) => legacy.PrintLegacy(s);
}

⚠️ Common Pitfalls & Mistakes

Adding business logic inside the adapter class. The adapter should only handle interface mapping and delegate calls.

questions.question: What is the primary purpose of the Adapter pattern?
questions.answer: To allow classes with incompatible interfaces to work together by wrapping one class interface.

questions.question: Can an adapter support two-way conversion?
questions.answer: Yes, if it implements both target interfaces and delegates calls in both directions.

topics.title: Decorator Pattern
topics.html:
Decorator Pattern

Course: Design Patterns

Attach additional responsibilities to an object dynamically, providing a flexible alternative to subclassing.

💡 Key Concepts

  • Wrapper pattern: Wrapping an object and providing matching method signatures.
  • Open/Closed principle: Adding features to objects without changing original classes.
  • Stacking decorators: Chaining multiple wrappers together (e.g. CompressionDecorator(EncryptionDecorator(FileStream))).

💻 Practical Code Example

C# / CODE BLOCK
public interface IMessage { string Send(); }
public class MessageDecorator : IMessage {
    private IMessage message;
    public MessageDecorator(IMessage m) => message = m;
    public virtual string Send() => message.Send();
}

⚠️ Common Pitfalls & Mistakes

Creating deep decorator chains that make debugging difficult when errors happen inside inner wrappers.

questions.question: How does Decorator differ from Inheritance?
questions.answer: Inheritance adds behavior at compile-time to all instances. Decorator attaches behavior dynamically at runtime to specific object instances.

questions.question: Give a real-world framework example of the Decorator pattern.
questions.answer: The System.IO.Stream pipeline, where you wrap streams with BufferedStream or CryptoStream.

topics.title: Facade Pattern
topics.html:
Facade Pattern

Course: Design Patterns

Provide a unified, simplified interface to a complex subsystem of classes.

💡 Key Concepts

  • Unified Interface: Exposing a single entry point method.
  • Subsystem Decoupling: Clients interact with the facade instead of managing multiple subsystem classes.
  • Simplify client calls: Hiding complex instantiation and method steps.

💻 Practical Code Example

C# / CODE BLOCK
public class MortgageFacade {
    private Bank bank = new Bank();
    private Credit credit = new Credit();
    public bool IsEligible(Customer c) => bank.HasSavings(c) && credit.HasClearHistory(c);
}

⚠️ Common Pitfalls & Mistakes

Making the Facade class too powerful, turning it into a "God Class" that contains subsystem business logic instead of just routing calls.

questions.question: What is the main goal of the Facade pattern?
questions.answer: To provide a simplified, single interface to a complex subsystem, making it easier to use.

questions.question: Does a Facade prevent clients from accessing subsystems directly?
questions.answer: No, clients can still access and use subsystem classes directly if they need advanced configurations.

topics.title: Proxy Pattern
topics.html:
Proxy Pattern

Course: Design Patterns

Provide a surrogate or placeholder for another object to control access, perform lazy loading, or cache requests.

💡 Key Concepts

  • Lazy Initialization (Virtual Proxy): Delaying initialization of expensive objects until they are needed.
  • Access Control (Protection Proxy): Verifying client permissions before delegating calls.
  • Caching (Cache Proxy): Storing query results to return matches without running expensive operations again.

💻 Practical Code Example

C# / CODE BLOCK
public class SecureDocumentProxy : IDocument {
    private RealDocument doc;
    public void Display(User u) {
        if (u.Role == "Admin") {
            doc ??= new RealDocument(); doc.Display(u);
        }
    }
}

⚠️ Common Pitfalls & Mistakes

Adding too many layers of proxy wrappers, which adds method call latency and complicates design.

questions.question: What is a Virtual Proxy?
questions.answer: A proxy that controls access to a resource that is expensive to create, instantiating it only when requested.

questions.question: How does Proxy differ from Decorator?
questions.answer: Proxy manages the lifecycle of its subject object. Decorator is passed its subject instance by the client.

topics.title: Composite & Flyweight Patterns
topics.html:
Composite & Flyweight Patterns

Course: Design Patterns

Treat single objects and collections uniformly using Composite, and share objects to save memory using Flyweight.

💡 Key Concepts

  • Composite Pattern: Groups objects into tree structures to represent part-whole hierarchies.
  • Flyweight Pattern: Shares fine-grained objects to support large quantities of objects efficiently.
  • Intrinsic vs Extrinsic State: Intrinsic state is shared (Flyweight). Extrinsic state depends on context.

💻 Practical Code Example

C# / CODE BLOCK
// Composite tree node
public interface IComponent { void Display(); }
public class Folder : IComponent {
    private List<IComponent> children = new List<IComponent>();
    public void Display() => children.ForEach(c => c.Display());
}

⚠️ Common Pitfalls & Mistakes

Making composite interfaces too generic, which forces leaf nodes to implement methods (like Add/Remove) they do not support.

questions.question: What is the goal of the Flyweight pattern?
questions.answer: To reduce memory usage by sharing common data across multiple objects instead of duplicating it.

questions.question: When should the Composite pattern be used?
questions.answer: When you need to treat single objects and composite groups of objects uniformly (like files and folders).

topics.title: Strategy Pattern
topics.html:
Strategy Pattern

Course: Design Patterns

Define a family of algorithms, encapsulate each one, and make them interchangeable at runtime.

💡 Key Concepts

  • Interchangeable algorithms: Selecting algorithms dynamically based on context.
  • Open/Closed principle: Adding new strategies without modifying existing context classes.
  • Abstractions: Strategies implement a shared interface contract.

💻 Practical Code Example

C# / CODE BLOCK
public interface ISortStrategy { void Sort(List<int> list); }
public class QuickSort : ISortStrategy { public void Sort(List<int> l) { } }
public class Context {
    private ISortStrategy strat;
    public void SetStrategy(ISortStrategy s) => strat = s;
    public void Execute(List<int> l) => strat.Sort(l);
}

⚠️ Common Pitfalls & Mistakes

Implementing Strategy when the algorithm never changes, adding unnecessary classes and interface overhead.

questions.question: How does the Strategy pattern implement the Open/Closed Principle?
questions.answer: By letting you introduce new algorithms (strategies) as separate classes without modifying the class that uses them.

questions.question: What is the difference between Strategy and State patterns?
questions.answer: In Strategy, the client selects the strategy. In State, the state transitions occur dynamically inside the context object based on its internal state.

topics.title: Observer Pattern
topics.html:
Observer Pattern

Course: Design Patterns

Create one-to-many subscription models where subject changes notify subscribing observer objects automatically.

💡 Key Concepts

  • Subject / Observable: Manages a list of observers and notifies them when state changes.
  • Observer: Subscribes to updates and implements an Update method.
  • Publish-Subscribe: Decoupled communication pattern where senders don't know specific receivers.

💻 Practical Code Example

C# / CODE BLOCK
public interface IObserver { void Update(string state); }
public class Subject {
    private List<IObserver> observers = new List<IObserver>();
    public void Notify(string state) => observers.ForEach(o => o.Update(state));
}

⚠️ Common Pitfalls & Mistakes

Forgetting to unsubscribe observers, which causes memory leaks because subjects retain references to deleted objects.

questions.question: How does the Observer pattern decouple objects?
questions.answer: The Subject only knows that observers implement a specific interface; it doesn't know the concrete classes or their internal workings.

questions.question: What is a memory leak hazard in the Observer pattern?
questions.answer: If observers do not unsubscribe when disposed, the Subject holds their references in memory, preventing garbage collection.

topics.title: Command Pattern
topics.html:
Command Pattern

Course: Design Patterns

Encapsulate requests as objects, allowing parameterization, queueing, and rollback logs.

💡 Key Concepts

  • Request Encapsulation: Wrapping an action and its parameters inside a class.
  • Undo / Redo: Implementing execution history and rollback methods (Unexecute()).
  • Invoker: The class that triggers the command execution.

💻 Practical Code Example

C# / CODE BLOCK
public interface ICommand { void Execute(); void Undo(); }
public class OpenCommand : ICommand {
    private Receiver receiver;
    public void Execute() => receiver.Open();
    public void Undo() => receiver.Close();
}

⚠️ Common Pitfalls & Mistakes

Creating a new command class for every single minor method call, resulting in class bloat in the project.

questions.question: How does the Command pattern support undo operations?
questions.answer: By storing the state required to reverse the action within the command object, and executing an Undo() method.

questions.question: What are the main components of the Command pattern?
questions.answer: The Client, Invoker, Command Interface, Concrete Command, and Receiver.

topics.title: State Pattern
topics.html:
State Pattern

Course: Design Patterns

Allow objects to alter their behavior dynamically when their internal state changes.

💡 Key Concepts

  • State Abstraction: Encapsulating state-specific behavior into separate state classes.
  • Context delegation: The context object delegates actions to the current state object.
  • Transitions: Changing the current state instance dynamically during execution.

💻 Practical Code Example

C# / CODE BLOCK
public interface IOrderState { void Process(OrderContext ctx); }
public class PlacedState : IOrderState {
    public void Process(OrderContext ctx) => ctx.State = new ShippedState();
}

⚠️ Common Pitfalls & Mistakes

Writing state transition logic in a way that creates tight coupling between concrete state classes.

questions.question: When is the State pattern useful?
questions.answer: When an object's behavior depends on its state, and its code contains massive conditional statements branching based on state values.

questions.question: Where should state transition logic be defined?
questions.answer: It can be defined either inside the context object, or inside the individual state classes, depending on the complexity.

topics.title: Chain of Responsibility
topics.html:
Chain of Responsibility

Course: Design Patterns

Pass requests along a chain of handlers, letting each handler process or pass the request to the next.

💡 Key Concepts

  • Handler Chain: A sequence of handler objects linked by references.
  • Request processing: Each handler decides to process the request or pass it to the next.
  • Decoupling Senders: The sender doesn't know which specific handler will process the request.

💻 Practical Code Example

C# / CODE BLOCK
public abstract class Handler {
    protected Handler next;
    public void SetNext(Handler h) => next = h;
    public abstract void HandleRequest(Request r);
}

⚠️ Common Pitfalls & Mistakes

Not handling the end of the chain, which can cause requests to fall off the chain and remain unprocessed.

questions.question: Give a framework example of the Chain of Responsibility pattern.
questions.answer: The HTTP middleware pipeline in ASP.NET Core, where each middleware handles or passes requests down the line.

questions.question: What is the risk of an unhandled request in this pattern?
questions.answer: The request may reach the end of the chain without being processed, resulting in silent failures.

topics.title: Template Method Pattern
topics.html:
Template Method Pattern

Course: Design Patterns

Define the skeleton of an algorithm in a base method, deferring some steps to subclasses without changing the algorithm's structure.

💡 Key Concepts

  • Algorithm Skeleton: The main method defines the execution steps.
  • Hook Methods: Abstract or virtual steps overridden in subclasses to customize behavior.
  • Inversion of Control: The parent class calls the subclass methods, not vice versa (Hollywood Principle).

💻 Practical Code Example

C# / CODE BLOCK
public abstract class DataParser {
    public void ParseData() {
        OpenConnection(); ReadData(); CloseConnection(); // Skeleton
    }
    protected abstract void ReadData();
}

⚠️ Common Pitfalls & Mistakes

Violating the Liskov Substitution Principle by overriding template steps in a way that breaks base class assumptions.

questions.question: What is the "Hollywood Principle" in Template Method?
questions.answer: "Don't call us, we'll call you"—the base class calls the subclass override methods at the correct execution step.

questions.question: How does Template Method differ from Strategy?
questions.answer: Template Method uses inheritance to vary parts of an algorithm. Strategy uses composition to swap the entire algorithm.

topics.title: Iterator & Mediator Patterns
topics.html:
Iterator & Mediator Patterns

Course: Design Patterns

Traverse collections sequentially using Iterator, and encapsulate complex object communications using Mediator.

💡 Key Concepts

  • Iterator Pattern: Accesses elements of a collection sequentially without exposing its internal structure.
  • Mediator Pattern: Reduces direct connections between classes by forcing them to communicate through a mediator.
  • MediatR library: A popular .NET package used to implement in-memory request/response dispatching.

💻 Practical Code Example

C# / CODE BLOCK
// Mediator interface snippet
public interface IMediator {
    void Send(string msg, Colleague colleague);
}

⚠️ Common Pitfalls & Mistakes

Creating a "God Mediator" that contains excessive coordination logic, making the mediator class difficult to maintain.

questions.question: What problem does the Mediator pattern solve?
questions.answer: It reduces direct references between tightly coupled classes (spaghetti code) by routing communication through a central mediator.

questions.question: How does the Iterator pattern help collections?
questions.answer: It provides a standard interface to traverse different collection types (lists, trees) without exposing their internal storage systems.

topics.title: Intro to EF Core & ORMs
topics.html:
Intro to EF Core & ORMs

Course: Entity Framework Core

Object-Relational Mappers (ORMs) bridge the gap between relational databases and object-oriented C# code, allowing developers to query database tables using objects.

💡 Key Concepts

  • Object-Relational Mapping: Mapping database tables to C# classes, and columns to properties.
  • Entity Framework Core: Microsoft's lightweight, cross-platform, open-source ORM for .NET.
  • SQL translation: Translates LINQ expressions into optimized SQL queries.

💻 Practical Code Example

C# / CODE BLOCK
using var db = new AppDbContext();
var users = db.Users.Where(u => u.IsActive).ToList(); // Translates to: SELECT * FROM Users WHERE IsActive = 1

⚠️ Common Pitfalls & Mistakes

Expecting ORM translation to handle complex C# functions inside database query expressions, resulting in runtime conversion errors.

questions.question: What is an ORM?
questions.answer: An Object-Relational Mapper is a tool that automates database mapping and operations, translating C# code into SQL.

questions.question: What is EF Core?
questions.answer: Microsoft's modern ORM framework for .NET, enabling databases to be queried and updated using C# objects.

topics.title: DbContext Configuration
topics.html:
DbContext Configuration

Course: Entity Framework Core

Configure connection strings, database providers, logging, and performance flags inside the DbContext class.

💡 Key Concepts

  • OnConfiguring: Method inside DbContext where connection settings are set.
  • Database Providers: Targeting specific engines (SQL Server, PostgreSQL, SQLite).
  • Logging SQL queries: Configuring output streams to print generated SQL commands in development.

💻 Practical Code Example

C# / CODE BLOCK
public class AppDbContext : DbContext {
    protected override void OnConfiguring(DbContextOptionsBuilder options)
        => options.UseSqlServer("Server=localhost;Database=TestDb;Trusted_Connection=True;")
                  .LogTo(Console.WriteLine, LogLevel.Information); // Logs SQL to console
}

⚠️ Common Pitfalls & Mistakes

Hardcoding database connection strings inside the DbContext class, which creates security risks and deployment challenges.

questions.question: Where should database connection strings be stored?
questions.answer: In configuration files (appsettings.json) and injected using Dependency Injection.

questions.question: What does the DbContextOptions class do?
questions.answer: It passes configuration settings (database provider, connection string, flags) into the DbContext constructor.

topics.title: DbSets & Entity States
topics.html:
DbSets & Entity States

Course: Entity Framework Core

DbSets represent queryable database tables. The DbContext tracks entity states to determine what SQL to run during SaveChanges().

💡 Key Concepts

  • DbSet: Represents a collection of specific entities mapped to a database table.
  • Entity States: Entities are tracked as Added, Unchanged, Modified, Deleted, or Detached.
  • SaveChanges: Scans the change tracker and executes matching SQL inserts, updates, and deletes.

💻 Practical Code Example

C# / CODE BLOCK
var user = context.Users.Find(1);
user.Name = "New Name"; // Tracker sets state to Modified
context.SaveChanges(); // Runs UPDATE SQL

⚠️ Common Pitfalls & Mistakes

Adding an entity to context but forgetting to call SaveChanges(), which leaves changes uncommitted.

questions.question: What is the purpose of the Detached state?
questions.answer: The entity is not being tracked by the DbContext, so changes made to it will not be saved during SaveChanges().

questions.question: How do you tell EF Core to track a new record?
questions.answer: By calling context.Add() or context.Set<T>().Add(), which sets the entity state to Added.

topics.title: Code-First vs Database-First
topics.html:
Code-First vs Database-First

Course: Entity Framework Core

Choose between building the database from C# classes (Code-First) or generating C# classes from an existing database schema (Database-First).

💡 Key Concepts

  • Code-First: Define entities in C# and run migrations to create or update the database.
  • Database-First: Use CLI scaffold commands to generate C# entities from an existing database.
  • Model synchronization: Keeping database schemas and application models in sync.

💻 Practical Code Example

C# / CODE BLOCK
// Database-First CLI Scaffolding command
// dotnet ef dbcontext scaffold "Server=localhost;Database=Db;" Microsoft.EntityFrameworkCore.SqlServer -o Models

⚠️ Common Pitfalls & Mistakes

Modifying scaffolded entity files manually in Database-First, which gets overwritten when running the scaffold command again.

questions.question: When is Code-First preferred over Database-First?
questions.answer: When you are building a new application and want to manage the database schema entirely in source control using C# migrations.

questions.question: How do you keep Code-First models synced with the database?
questions.answer: By creating and applying database migrations using ef CLI commands.

topics.title: Fluent API vs Data Annotations
topics.html:
Fluent API vs Data Annotations

Course: Entity Framework Core

Map entity properties to database columns using Data Annotation attributes or the Fluent API inside OnModelCreating.

💡 Key Concepts

  • Data Annotations: Attributes applied directly to entity properties ([Key], [Required]).
  • Fluent API: Method-chaining syntax declared inside DbContext OnModelCreating.
  • Advanced Configs: Fluent API supports composite keys, unique indexes, and cascade delete rules.

💻 Practical Code Example

C# / CODE BLOCK
protected override void OnModelCreating(ModelBuilder modelBuilder) {
    modelBuilder.Entity<User>()
        .HasIndex(u => u.Email)
        .IsUnique(); // Unique Index via Fluent API
}

⚠️ Common Pitfalls & Mistakes

Mixing Fluent API and Data Annotations inconsistently, making database schema rules hard to locate.

questions.question: Why is Fluent API preferred for complex databases?
questions.answer: Because it keeps entity models clean of database metadata and supports complex configurations like composite keys and unique indexes.

questions.question: Which overrides which: Data Annotations or Fluent API?
questions.answer: Fluent API configurations override Data Annotations when there are conflicting rules.

topics.title: Migrations & Schema Seeding
topics.html:
Migrations & Schema Seeding

Course: Entity Framework Core

Apply database migrations incrementally to track schema changes, and seed tables with default database records.

💡 Key Concepts

  • Add-Migration: Generates migration files describing Up() and Down() schema changes.
  • Database-Update: Applies pending migrations to target databases.
  • Model Seeding: Adding default values (like admin accounts or lookup tables) in OnModelCreating.

💻 Practical Code Example

C# / CODE BLOCK
protected override void OnModelCreating(ModelBuilder modelBuilder) {
    modelBuilder.Entity<Role>().HasData(
        new Role { Id = 1, Name = "Admin" } // Data Seeding
    );
}

⚠️ Common Pitfalls & Mistakes

Manually editing database tables directly in production, which breaks migration sequence tracking.

questions.question: What is the role of Up and Down methods in migrations?
questions.answer: Up applies schema changes when updating the database. Down reverts those changes when rolling back.

questions.question: How do you seed database lookup data in EF Core?
questions.answer: Use the HasData() method inside OnModelCreating during model builder configuration.

topics.title: Querying Data (LINQ to Entities)
topics.html:
Querying Data (LINQ to Entities)

Course: Entity Framework Core

Write LINQ queries that EF Core translates into optimized SQL commands to query database records.

💡 Key Concepts

  • Expression Trees: EF Core parses LINQ queries as Expression Trees to translate them to SQL.
  • Client vs Server Evaluation: EF Core executes filters on the database server, bringing only matching records to memory.
  • Immediate execution methods: ToList(), First(), and Count() trigger immediate database execution.

💻 Practical Code Example

C# / CODE BLOCK
var users = context.Users.Where(u => u.Age > 21).OrderBy(u => u.Name).ToList();

⚠️ Common Pitfalls & Mistakes

Adding functions in LINQ queries (like user.Birthday.ToString()) that cannot be translated to SQL, causing runtime failures.

questions.question: What happens when a LINQ expression cannot be translated to SQL?
questions.answer: EF Core throws an InvalidOperationException indicating that client evaluation is required.

questions.question: What is the difference between Single() and First() in querying?
questions.answer: First() returns the first matched item. Single() verifies that only one item matches the condition, throwing an exception if there are more.

topics.title: Related Data Loading Styles (Eager, Explicit, Lazy)
topics.html:
Related Data Loading Styles (Eager, Explicit, Lazy)

Course: Entity Framework Core

Load related objects from database tables using Eager Loading, Explicit Loading, or Lazy Loading.

💡 Key Concepts

  • Eager Loading (.Include): Pulls related data in the initial query using SQL JOINs.
  • Explicit Loading (.Load): Queries related records explicitly from the database for a loaded object.
  • Lazy Loading (virtual): Pushes database queries automatically when virtual navigation properties are accessed.

💻 Practical Code Example

C# / CODE BLOCK
var users = context.Users.Include(u => u.Orders).ToList(); // Eager Loading
var orders = context.Entry(singleUser).Collection(u => u.Orders).Query().ToList(); // Explicit Loading

⚠️ Common Pitfalls & Mistakes

Using Lazy Loading without caution, leading to the N+1 query problem by running database queries inside loops.

questions.question: What is the N+1 query problem?
questions.answer: An issue where accessing related data in a loop triggers separate database queries for every item in the list, hurting performance.

questions.question: What keyword enables Lazy Loading in entity classes?
questions.answer: The virtual keyword must be applied to navigation properties, and lazy loading proxies must be enabled in context.

topics.title: Tracking vs No-Tracking Queries
topics.html:
Tracking vs No-Tracking Queries

Course: Entity Framework Core

Save memory and CPU cycles by disabling the change tracker for read-only database queries.

💡 Key Concepts

  • AsNoTracking(): Disables tracking for the returned records, skipping change tracking checks.
  • Memory Overhead: Tracking queries keep copies of object states in memory, which uses more RAM.
  • Performance benefits: No-tracking queries run faster because they bypass entity state management.

💻 Practical Code Example

C# / CODE BLOCK
var readOnlyUsers = context.Users.AsNoTracking().Where(u => u.IsActive).ToList();

⚠️ Common Pitfalls & Mistakes

Attempting to save changes to an entity fetched using AsNoTracking() without attaching it back to the tracker first.

questions.question: When should you use AsNoTracking()?
questions.answer: For read-only queries where returned data will not be updated or saved back to the database.

questions.question: Can you save updates to an entity fetched with AsNoTracking?
questions.answer: Yes, but you must attach it back using context.Update() or context.Attach() to track changes.

topics.title: CRUD operations & DbContext State
topics.html:
CRUD operations & DbContext State

Course: Entity Framework Core

Perform Create, Read, Update, and Delete operations using Add, Remove, and property assignment patterns.

💡 Key Concepts

  • Add: Registers a new record, marking its state as Added.
  • Update: Attaches an entity and marks all its properties as Modified.
  • Remove: Marks the tracked entity state as Deleted for removal during SaveChanges().

💻 Practical Code Example

C# / CODE BLOCK
var u = new User() { Name = "John" };
context.Users.Add(u); // Added
context.SaveChanges(); // INSERT

context.Users.Remove(u); // Deleted
context.SaveChanges(); // DELETE

⚠️ Common Pitfalls & Mistakes

Calling Update() unnecessarily for tracked entities. If the object is tracked, changing its properties is automatically detected, so calling Update() is redundant.

questions.question: Does context.Remove() immediately delete the row?
questions.answer: No, it only marks the entity state as Deleted. The SQL DELETE command runs only when SaveChanges() is executed.

questions.question: What does calling Update() do to untracked entities?
questions.answer: It attaches the entity to the context and marks its state as Modified, telling SaveChanges() to update all fields.

topics.title: Concurrency Conflict Handling
topics.html:
Concurrency Conflict Handling

Course: Entity Framework Core

Handle multi-user concurrency updates using optimistic concurrency checks (tokens and rowversions).

💡 Key Concepts

  • Optimistic Concurrency: Assumes conflict is rare. Verifies rowversion values before writing updates.
  • Concurrency Token: Properties marked with [ConcurrencyCheck] or rowversion columns.
  • DbUpdateConcurrencyException: Exception thrown when another user updated the row first.

💻 Practical Code Example

C# / CODE BLOCK
try {
    context.SaveChanges();
} catch (DbUpdateConcurrencyException ex) {
    var entry = ex.Entries.Single();
    entry.OriginalValues.SetValues(entry.GetDatabaseValues()); // Database wins or Client wins resolution
}

⚠️ Common Pitfalls & Mistakes

Not handling DbUpdateConcurrencyException, which crashes the app when two users update the same row simultaneously.

questions.question: How is concurrency managed in EF Core?
questions.answer: Through optimistic concurrency using RowVersion or concurrency tokens to verify columns have not changed since loading.

questions.question: What is a database-wins resolution?
questions.answer: Updating the client-loaded entity values with the values currently in the database, overriding client modifications.

topics.title: Transactions & Savepoints
topics.html:
Transactions & Savepoints

Course: Entity Framework Core

Group multiple SaveChanges calls into single atomic transactions, and configure rollback savepoints.

💡 Key Concepts

  • Database Transactions: Ensuring all operations succeed or roll back together (BeginTransaction).
  • Savepoints: Markers within a transaction to allow partial rollbacks.
  • Isolation Levels: Setting database locks behavior during transaction execution.

💻 Practical Code Example

C# / CODE BLOCK
using var transaction = context.Database.BeginTransaction();
try {
    context.SaveChanges();
    transaction.Commit();
} catch {
    transaction.Rollback();
}

⚠️ Common Pitfalls & Mistakes

Not using transactions when updating related records across multiple DbContext calls, risking partial database saves.

questions.question: When is BeginTransaction required in EF Core?
questions.answer: When you are coordinating database operations across multiple SaveChanges() calls or integrating external database actions.

questions.question: What are savepoints in transactions?
questions.answer: Markers that allow you to roll back a transaction to a specific point, retaining operations made before the savepoint.

topics.title: Performance Tuning & Index Maps
topics.html:
Performance Tuning & Index Maps

Course: Entity Framework Core

Optimize EF Core performance using compiled queries, connection pooling, and indexing strategies.

💡 Key Concepts

  • DbContext Pooling: Reuses DbContext instances to avoid construction overhead.
  • Compiled Queries: Caches query translations to speed up repetitive database calls.
  • Query Splitting: Splitting large queries into separate SQL queries to prevent Cartesian explosion.

💻 Practical Code Example

C# / CODE BLOCK
builder.Services.AddDbContextPool<AppDbContext>(options => 
    options.UseSqlServer(connectionString)); // Context pooling

⚠️ Common Pitfalls & Mistakes

Using .Include() on many nested collections, which generates complex JOIN queries that slow down the database.

questions.question: What is DbContext Pooling?
questions.answer: A feature that reuses pre-created DbContext instances from a pool, reducing thread overhead during app startup.

questions.question: How does Query Splitting solve Cartesian explosion?
questions.answer: By sending separate SQL queries to fetch related data instead of a single query with multiple JOINs, reducing duplicate data.

topics.title: Shadow Properties & Global Filters
topics.html:
Shadow Properties & Global Filters

Course: Entity Framework Core

Implement soft deletes and multi-tenant security using shadow properties and global query filters.

💡 Key Concepts

  • Shadow Properties: Properties defined in EF Core metadata that do not exist in the C# class.
  • Global Query Filters: Query filters applied to entities automatically (e.g., HasQueryFilter).
  • Soft Deletes: Setting an IsDeleted flag instead of deleting database rows.

💻 Practical Code Example

C# / CODE BLOCK
modelBuilder.Entity<Product>()
    .HasQueryFilter(p => !p.IsDeleted); // Global Filter

modelBuilder.Entity<Product>()
    .Property<DateTime>("LastUpdated"); // Shadow Property

⚠️ Common Pitfalls & Mistakes

Forgetting how to bypass global query filters when you need to load deleted records (requires using IgnoreQueryFilters()).

questions.question: What is a Shadow Property?
questions.answer: A property that exists in the database table and EF Core model, but has no matching field in the C# entity class.

questions.question: How do you bypass a global query filter?
questions.answer: By applying the IgnoreQueryFilters() extension method to the query.

topics.title: Interceptors and DbContext Events
topics.html:
Interceptors and DbContext Events

Course: Entity Framework Core

Intercept database commands and execution states to automate auditing, logging, and data modifications.

💡 Key Concepts

  • Interceptors: Classes that run code before or after database commands (SaveChangesInterceptor).
  • SavedChanges Event: Subscribing to notifications after data is saved.
  • Auditing data: Automatically updating CreatedDate or UpdatedBy fields.

💻 Practical Code Example

C# / CODE BLOCK
public class AuditInterceptor : SaveChangesInterceptor {
    public override InterceptionResult<int> SavingChanges(
        DbContextEventData eventData, InterceptionResult<int> result) {
        // Audit logic: Set UpdatedDate
        return base.SavingChanges(eventData, result);
    }
}

⚠️ Common Pitfalls & Mistakes

Adding slow, block-heavy code inside interceptors, which adds latency to every database command.

questions.question: What is an EF Core Interceptor?
questions.answer: A class that hooks into database execution steps, allowing commands to be modified or monitored before they run.

questions.question: How do you automate setting CreatedBy audit properties?
questions.answer: By overriding SavingChanges or using a SaveChangesInterceptor to scan tracked entities for audit interfaces.

topics.title: Testing with In-Memory & SQLite
topics.html:
Testing with In-Memory & SQLite

Course: Entity Framework Core

Unit test database logic using the EF Core In-Memory provider or local SQLite databases.

💡 Key Concepts

  • In-Memory Database: A fast, lightweight RAM provider. Does not enforce relational constraints.
  • SQLite In-Memory: A relational in-memory database that enforces foreign keys and index rules.
  • Test Isolation: Creating a new database instance per unit test to prevent data overlap.

💻 Practical Code Example

C# / CODE BLOCK
var options = new DbContextOptionsBuilder<AppDbContext>()
    .UseInMemoryDatabase(databaseName: "TestDb")
    .Options;
using var context = new AppDbContext(options);

⚠️ Common Pitfalls & Mistakes

Using the In-Memory provider to test raw SQL queries or database-specific features (like JSON query extensions).

questions.question: Why is SQLite preferred over the In-Memory provider for testing?
questions.answer: Because SQLite is a real relational database that enforces constraints, whereas the In-Memory provider does not check relations or indexes.

questions.question: How do you ensure test isolation when database testing?
questions.answer: By creating a fresh in-memory database name or connection instance per test run.

topics.title: Introduction to LINQ
topics.html:
Introduction to LINQ

Course: LINQ

LINQ (Language Integrated Query) brings declarative querying directly into C#, allowing data to be filtered, sorted, and mapped.

💡 Key Concepts

  • Declarative Querying: Write readable query logic instead of nested loop statements.
  • LINQ Providers: Targets different sources: LINQ to Objects, LINQ to SQL, and LINQ to XML.
  • Extension Methods: Methods like Where and Select that extend collections.

💻 Practical Code Example

C# / CODE BLOCK
string[] names = { "Tom", "Dick", "Harry" };
var matched = names.Where(n => n.Length == 3);
// Returns Tom, Dick

⚠️ Common Pitfalls & Mistakes

Assuming LINQ makes queries run faster. LINQ is a syntax compiler helper; it does not bypass the performance of underlying loops.

questions.question: What does LINQ stand for?
questions.answer: Language Integrated Query, a feature adding declarative query capabilities to C#.

questions.question: What is a LINQ Provider?
questions.answer: A library that translates LINQ expressions into queries for specific data sources, like databases or XML.

topics.title: IEnumerable vs IQueryable vs IOrderedEnumerable
topics.html:
IEnumerable vs IQueryable vs IOrderedEnumerable

Course: LINQ

Understand the difference between querying in-memory collections (IEnumerable) and generating database queries (IQueryable).

💡 Key Concepts

  • IEnumerable: Ideal for in-memory collections. Filters records client-side using delegates.
  • IQueryable: Ideal for database sources. Translates expression trees into SQL queries.
  • IOrderedEnumerable: Returned by OrderBy calls, allowing subsequent ThenBy ordering.

💻 Practical Code Example

C# / CODE BLOCK
IEnumerable<User> inMemory = GetUsersList().Where(u => u.Age > 18); // In-memory
IQueryable<User> dbQuery = dbContext.Users.Where(u => u.Age > 18); // Translates to SQL

⚠️ Common Pitfalls & Mistakes

Casting an IQueryable query to IEnumerable before filtering, which pulls all table rows into memory before applying the filter.

questions.question: What is the main difference between IEnumerable and IQueryable?
questions.answer: IEnumerable is for in-memory queries (in-process). IQueryable parses query expressions to run them on external sources like databases.

questions.question: Why is casting to IEnumerable mid-query bad for databases?
questions.answer: It causes EF Core to execute the SQL immediately and pull all records into memory, running subsequent filters locally.

topics.title: Deferred vs Immediate Execution
topics.html:
Deferred vs Immediate Execution

Course: LINQ

Understand when LINQ queries are evaluated: deferred iteration vs immediate materialization.

💡 Key Concepts

  • Deferred execution: The query builds a pipeline but does not run until you iterate over it.
  • Immediate execution: Methods like ToList(), Count(), and First() run the query immediately.
  • Query reuse: A deferred query can be rerun after modifying the underlying collection.

💻 Practical Code Example

C# / CODE BLOCK
var list = new List<int> { 1, 2 };
var query = list.Where(x => x > 1); // Deferred
list.Add(3);
foreach (var v in query) Console.WriteLine(v); // Outputs 2, 3

⚠️ Common Pitfalls & Mistakes

Running database queries multiple times by iterating over a deferred LINQ query in a loop instead of calling ToList().

questions.question: What is deferred execution?
questions.answer: The query is evaluated only when the query variable is iterated or converted, not when defined.

questions.question: How do you force immediate execution of a LINQ query?
questions.answer: By calling collection conversion methods like ToList(), ToArray(), or ToDictionary().

topics.title: Query Syntax vs Method Syntax
topics.html:
Query Syntax vs Method Syntax

Course: LINQ

Compare declarative Query syntax (from-select) with functional Method syntax (lambda extensions).

💡 Key Concepts

  • Query Syntax: Looks like SQL. Compiled into equivalent method syntax.
  • Method Syntax: Uses extension methods and lambdas. Required for operators like Skip or Take.
  • Readability: Query syntax is often easier to read for complex joins and groupings.

💻 Practical Code Example

C# / CODE BLOCK
// Query Syntax
var q1 = from u in users where u.Active select u.Name;

// Method Syntax (Equivalent)
var q2 = users.Where(u => u.Active).Select(u => u.Name);

⚠️ Common Pitfalls & Mistakes

Mixing query and method syntax in a confusing way, making the code hard to read.

questions.question: Which syntax is compiled into the other?
questions.answer: The compiler translates Query syntax into Method syntax extension calls before compilation.

questions.question: When is Method syntax required?
questions.answer: For operators that do not have query keywords, such as Take, Skip, First, or ToList.

topics.title: Filtering Operators (Where, OfType)
topics.html:
Filtering Operators (Where, OfType)

Course: LINQ

Filter data streams based on conditions or object type structures.

💡 Key Concepts

  • Where: Filters items using a boolean condition.
  • OfType: Filters a collection, returning only objects of the specified type T.
  • Predicate matching: Using expressions to filter records.

💻 Practical Code Example

C# / CODE BLOCK
object[] items = { "Tom", 2, "Harry", 4 };
var strings = items.OfType<string>(); // Returns Tom, Harry

⚠️ Common Pitfalls & Mistakes

Using OfType() with database tables when table structures are not mapped to class inheritance, causing translation failures.

questions.question: What does OfType<T>() do?
questions.answer: It filters a collection, returning only the elements that match the specified type T.

questions.question: Can you write multiple conditions in a single Where clause?
questions.answer: Yes, using logical operators (&&, ||) inside the lambda expression.

topics.title: Projection Operators (Select, SelectMany)
topics.html:
Projection Operators (Select, SelectMany)

Course: LINQ

Project source records into new shapes, and flatten nested lists using Select and SelectMany.

💡 Key Concepts

  • Select (1-to-1): Transforms each source element into a new object shape.
  • SelectMany (1-to-Many): Projects and flattens nested lists of lists into a single collection.
  • Anonymous Types: Creating temporary classes to hold selected columns.

💻 Practical Code Example

C# / CODE BLOCK
var names = users.Select(u => u.Name); // List of strings
var allOrders = users.SelectMany(u => u.Orders); // Flattens orders lists

⚠️ Common Pitfalls & Mistakes

Using Select when SelectMany is needed, resulting in a nested collection (IEnumerable>) instead of a flat list (IEnumerable).

questions.question: What is the difference between Select and SelectMany?
questions.answer: Select transforms elements individually. SelectMany flattens nested collections into a single sequence.

questions.question: What is projection?
questions.answer: The process of selecting columns or transforming objects into new shapes (like DTOs or anonymous types).

topics.title: Sorting Operators (OrderBy, ThenBy)
topics.html:
Sorting Operators (OrderBy, ThenBy)

Course: LINQ

Sort elements in ascending or descending order, and chain multiple sorting rules.

💡 Key Concepts

  • OrderBy: Sorts elements in ascending order by a key.
  • OrderByDescending: Sorts elements in descending order.
  • ThenBy: Applies subsequent sorting rules to items that had matching keys in OrderBy.

💻 Practical Code Example

C# / CODE BLOCK
var sorted = users.OrderBy(u => u.LastName)
                   .ThenBy(u => u.FirstName);

⚠️ Common Pitfalls & Mistakes

Chaining multiple OrderBy calls (e.g. OrderBy().OrderBy()), which resets the sorting instead of using ThenBy().

questions.question: Why is OrderBy followed by another OrderBy incorrect?
questions.answer: Because the second OrderBy resets the sorting of the list, ignoring the first sorting rule. Use ThenBy instead.

questions.question: What does ThenBy do?
questions.answer: It performs a secondary sort on elements that had matching values in the primary sort.

topics.title: Joining Operators (Join, GroupJoin)
topics.html:
Joining Operators (Join, GroupJoin)

Course: LINQ

Join collections based on matching keys, implementing SQL-like Inner and Outer joins.

💡 Key Concepts

  • Join: Correlates two sequences based on matching keys (Inner Join).
  • GroupJoin: Correlates sequences, grouping matching records by key (Left Outer Join).
  • Key Selectors: Defining columns to match from the left and right sequences.

💻 Practical Code Example

C# / CODE BLOCK
var joined = users.Join(orders, u => u.Id, o => o.UserId,
    (u, o) => new { u.Name, o.Total });

⚠️ Common Pitfalls & Mistakes

Using Join on in-memory collections with slow key comparisons, which hurts performance on large lists.

questions.question: What is the SQL equivalent of GroupJoin?
questions.answer: A LEFT OUTER JOIN, which groups matching right-side records for each left-side record.

questions.question: How does Join relate keys?
questions.answer: It compares keys from the outer and inner sequences, outputting matches based on key equality.

topics.title: Grouping Operators (GroupBy, ToLookup)
topics.html:
Grouping Operators (GroupBy, ToLookup)

Course: LINQ

Group elements in collections by keys, and compare deferred GroupBy queries with immediate Lookup cache.

💡 Key Concepts

  • GroupBy: Groups elements into key-value pairs (deferred execution).
  • ToLookup: Creates an in-memory dictionary-like lookup cache (immediate execution).
  • IGrouping: The interface returned by grouping queries, containing Key and collection values.

💻 Practical Code Example

C# / CODE BLOCK
var grouped = users.GroupBy(u => u.Role);
// Each group has .Key (Role) and can be iterated as a list of Users

⚠️ Common Pitfalls & Mistakes

Assuming GroupBy behaves like SQL Group By, which aggregates rows. LINQ GroupBy groups objects into nested lists, not flat summaries.

questions.question: What is the difference between GroupBy and ToLookup?
questions.answer: GroupBy is deferred. ToLookup executes immediately, creating a cached lookup table in memory.

questions.question: What type of structure does GroupBy return?
questions.answer: An IEnumerable of IGrouping<TKey, TElement> objects.

topics.title: Set Operators (Union, Intersect, Except)
topics.html:
Set Operators (Union, Intersect, Except)

Course: LINQ

Combine collections using set logic: Union, Intersect, Except, and Distinct.

💡 Key Concepts

  • Distinct: Filters out duplicate values from a sequence.
  • Union: Combines two sequences, removing duplicate values.
  • Intersect / Except: Intersect finds common items. Except filters out matching items.

💻 Practical Code Example

C# / CODE BLOCK
int[] seq1 = { 1, 2, 2, 3 };
var unique = seq1.Distinct(); // 1, 2, 3
int[] seq2 = { 3, 4 };
var combined = seq1.Union(seq2); // 1, 2, 3, 4

⚠️ Common Pitfalls & Mistakes

Using set operators on custom objects without implementing IEquatable or providing a custom IEqualityComparer, which prevents duplicates from being detected.

questions.question: Why does Distinct() not filter duplicate objects by default?
questions.answer: Because default object comparisons check reference equality. You must override GetHashCode/Equals or pass an IEqualityComparer.

questions.question: What is the difference between Union and Concat?
questions.answer: Union combines lists and removes duplicates. Concat appends lists together, retaining duplicates.

topics.title: Element Operators (First, Single, ElementAt)
topics.html:
Element Operators (First, Single, ElementAt)

Course: LINQ

Query single elements from sequences using First, Single, Last, and ElementAt operators.

💡 Key Concepts

  • First / FirstOrDefault: Returns the first match. Default versions return null/default if no match is found.
  • Single / SingleOrDefault: Returns the only match. Throws if multiple items match.
  • ElementAt: Retrieves the element at a specific index location.

💻 Practical Code Example

C# / CODE BLOCK
var firstAdmin = users.FirstOrDefault(u => u.Role == "Admin");
var singleOwner = users.SingleOrDefault(u => u.Role == "Owner");

⚠️ Common Pitfalls & Mistakes

Calling First() on an empty collection, which throws an InvalidOperationException. Best practice is to use FirstOrDefault() and check for null.

questions.question: When should SingleOrDefault() be used instead of FirstOrDefault()?
questions.answer: When it is a validation error for more than one item to match the condition (e.g. searching by unique email).

questions.question: What does FirstOrDefault() return if a collection is empty?
questions.answer: It returns the default value for the type (null for reference types, or zero/default for value types).

topics.title: Aggregation Operators (Count, Average, Aggregate)
topics.html:
Aggregation Operators (Count, Average, Aggregate)

Course: LINQ

Compute summaries over collections: Count, Sum, Min, Max, Average, and custom Aggregations.

💡 Key Concepts

  • Basic Aggregations: Methods like Count(), Sum(), Min(), and Max() to summarize values.
  • Average: Calculates the arithmetic mean of numeric properties.
  • Aggregate: Performs custom accumulator calculations (like reducing values).

💻 Practical Code Example

C# / CODE BLOCK
int[] nums = { 1, 2, 3, 4 };
int sum = nums.Sum(); // 10
string combined = nums.Select(n => n.ToString())
                      .Aggregate((a, b) => a + "," + b); // "1,2,3,4"

⚠️ Common Pitfalls & Mistakes

Calling Min() or Max() on an empty collection, which throws an InvalidOperationException.

questions.question: What is the purpose of the Aggregate operator?
questions.answer: It runs a custom accumulator function over a sequence, reducing the collection to a single value.

questions.question: Does calling Count() on a List run a database query?
questions.answer: If called on List<T>, it uses the List.Count property instantly. If called on IQueryable, it runs a SELECT COUNT SQL query.

topics.title: Partitioning Operators (Take, Skip)
topics.html:
Partitioning Operators (Take, Skip)

Course: LINQ

Split collections for pagination using Take, Skip, TakeWhile, and SkipWhile operators.

💡 Key Concepts

  • Take: Selects the first N elements of a sequence.
  • Skip: Skips the first N elements and returns the remaining elements.
  • TakeWhile / SkipWhile: Skips/Takes elements as long as a condition evaluates to true.

💻 Practical Code Example

C# / CODE BLOCK
// Page 3 query (assuming 10 items per page)
var page3 = users.Skip(20).Take(10).ToList();

⚠️ Common Pitfalls & Mistakes

Calling Skip() without an OrderBy, which can return inconsistent results from databases because relational table orders are not guaranteed.

questions.question: How is database pagination implemented in LINQ?
questions.answer: By combining Skip((pageNumber - 1) * pageSize) and Take(pageSize) on sorted queries.

questions.question: What is the difference between Take and TakeWhile?
questions.answer: Take selects a fixed number of items. TakeWhile selects items dynamically as long as a condition remains true, stopping at the first failure.

topics.title: Generation Operators (Range, Repeat, Empty)
topics.html:
Generation Operators (Range, Repeat, Empty)

Course: LINQ

Create dummy data sequences using Enumerable.Range, Enumerable.Repeat, and Enumerable.Empty.

💡 Key Concepts

  • Enumerable.Range: Generates a sequence of integers within a specified range.
  • Enumerable.Repeat: Generates a sequence containing one repeated value.
  • Enumerable.Empty: Returns an empty, cached IEnumerable sequence, avoiding allocation.

💻 Practical Code Example

C# / CODE BLOCK
var range = Enumerable.Range(1, 10); // 1, 2... 10
var repeated = Enumerable.Repeat("Draft", 3); // Draft, Draft, Draft

⚠️ Common Pitfalls & Mistakes

Allocating new empty arrays instead of using Enumerable.Empty(), which wastes memory allocations in API pipelines.

questions.question: Why is Enumerable.Empty<T>() preferred over creating empty arrays?
questions.answer: Because it returns a cached internal singleton instance, avoiding memory allocation overhead.

questions.question: What are the arguments for Enumerable.Range(start, count)?
questions.answer: The first argument is the starting integer. The second is the count of sequential integers to generate.

topics.title: Custom Operators & Expression Trees
topics.html:
Custom Operators & Expression Trees

Course: LINQ

Build custom query extensions and work with Expression Trees to translate custom syntax into database commands.

💡 Key Concepts

  • Custom Extensions: Creating custom LINQ query methods using "this IEnumerable" syntax.
  • Expression Trees: Representing code structures as data nodes (Expression>) to parse at runtime.
  • Query Translation: How ORM providers parse expressions to generate SQL.

💻 Practical Code Example

C# / CODE BLOCK
// Expression parameter matching
Expression<Func<User, bool>> expr = u => u.Age > 18;
ParameterExpression param = expr.Parameters[0]; // Parses "u" as parameter node

⚠️ Common Pitfalls & Mistakes

Failing to differentiate between Func (compiled delegate code) and Expression> (data structure representing code), which disables database translation.

questions.question: What is an Expression Tree?
questions.answer: A data structure that represents a compiler expression in a tree layout, allowing runtime analysis and translation (e.g. to SQL).

questions.question: Why does EF Core accept Expression<Func<T, bool>> instead of Func<T, bool>?
questions.answer: Because it needs to inspect the query structure to write SQL. A Func is compiled binary code, which cannot be inspected or translated.

topics.title: Intro to Real-Time Web & SignalR
topics.html:
Intro to Real-Time Web & SignalR

Course: SignalR

ASP.NET Core SignalR simplifies adding real-time web functionality, allowing server-side code to push content to connected clients instantly.

💡 Key Concepts

  • Real-Time Web: Enables instant updates without browser page reloads.
  • Bidirectional Connection: Both client and server can send messages simultaneously.
  • Connection Fallback: Automatically selects the best communication channel (WebSockets, SSE, or Long Polling).

💻 Practical Code Example

C# / CODE BLOCK
// In Program.cs
builder.Services.AddSignalR();
// ...
app.MapHub<ChatHub>("/chat");

⚠️ Common Pitfalls & Mistakes

Assuming SignalR is only for chat apps. It is ideal for dashboards, status feeds, and collaborative editors.

questions.question: What does SignalR do?
questions.answer: It manages connections and allows real-time, bi-directional communication between client and server.

questions.question: What is connection fallback?
questions.answer: The automatic process where SignalR falls back to simpler protocols if WebSockets are blocked by proxies or networks.

topics.title: Hub Architecture & Remote Procedure Calls
topics.html:
Hub Architecture & Remote Procedure Calls

Course: SignalR

Hubs are the high-level communications pipeline in SignalR that let servers and clients invoke methods on each other.

💡 Key Concepts

  • Hub Class: Inherits from Hub, acting as the endpoint for client actions.
  • Remote Procedure Calls (RPC): Executing functions across the network as if they were local.
  • Clients Property: Specifies which connected clients receive the message.

💻 Practical Code Example

C# / CODE BLOCK
public class ChatHub : Hub {
    public async Task SendMessage(string user, string msg) {
        await Clients.All.SendAsync("ReceiveMessage", user, msg);
    }
}

⚠️ Common Pitfalls & Mistakes

Storing state variables (like connection lists) directly in Hub instances. Hub classes are transient and recreated for every request.

questions.question: What is an RPC in SignalR?
questions.answer: Remote Procedure Call, allowing a client to call a server method or a server to invoke a client function.

questions.question: How is connection state maintained in Hubs?
questions.answer: Hubs are stateless. State must be managed in external databases, memory caches, or services.

topics.title: Transports (WebSockets, SSE, Long Polling)
topics.html:
Transports (WebSockets, SSE, Long Polling)

Course: SignalR

Understand the three transports used by SignalR under the hood: WebSockets, Server-Sent Events, and Long Polling.

💡 Key Concepts

  • WebSockets: The only true full-duplex, persistent connection. Recommended for performance.
  • Server-Sent Events (SSE): The server pushes updates over an HTTP connection; the client sends actions separately.
  • Long Polling: Standard HTTP requests held open by the server until data is ready.

💻 Practical Code Example

C# / CODE BLOCK
// Client-side forcing specific transport type
const connection = new signalR.HubConnectionBuilder()
    .withUrl("/chat", { transport: signalR.HttpTransportType.WebSockets })
    .build();

⚠️ Common Pitfalls & Mistakes

Not configuring WebSockets on the hosting server, forcing the app to fall back to Long Polling and causing high connection load.

questions.question: Why is WebSockets the preferred transport?
questions.answer: Because it establishes a single, low-latency, full-duplex TCP connection, reducing HTTP overhead.

questions.question: When is Server-Sent Events used?
questions.answer: When WebSockets are blocked but the browser supports persistent HTTP read streams.

topics.title: Connection Lifecycles & State Management
topics.html:
Connection Lifecycles & State Management

Course: SignalR

Manage connections as they connect, disconnect, or drop, and track connection IDs.

💡 Key Concepts

  • OnConnectedAsync: Event handler triggered when a new client connects.
  • OnDisconnectedAsync: Event handler triggered when a client disconnects.
  • ConnectionId: A unique string identifier assigned to each connection.

💻 Practical Code Example

C# / CODE BLOCK
public override async Task OnConnectedAsync() {
    string id = Context.ConnectionId;
    // Log or track connection
    await base.OnConnectedAsync();
}

⚠️ Common Pitfalls & Mistakes

Assuming ConnectionId is permanent. It resets whenever a client reconnects or refreshes the page.

questions.question: How do you detect when a user disconnects in SignalR?
questions.answer: By overriding the OnDisconnectedAsync(Exception ex) method in the Hub class.

questions.question: Does a page refresh preserve the ConnectionId?
questions.answer: No, a page refresh terminates the old connection and creates a new one with a different ConnectionId.

topics.title: Message Targets (All, User, Groups, Caller)
topics.html:
Message Targets (All, User, Groups, Caller)

Course: SignalR

Route messages to target audiences: all clients, a specific user, groups, or back to the caller.

💡 Key Concepts

  • Clients.All: Sends messages to all connected clients.
  • Clients.User: Sends messages to a specific user based on user identity claims.
  • Clients.Groups: Sends messages to custom named categories.

💻 Practical Code Example

C# / CODE BLOCK
public async Task AlertGroup(string group) {
    await Clients.Group(group).SendAsync("ShowAlert", "System Update");
}

⚠️ Common Pitfalls & Mistakes

Sending sensitive messages to Clients.All, risking data exposure to unauthorized clients.

questions.question: How does Clients.User differ from Clients.Client?
questions.answer: Clients.Client targets a single ConnectionId. Clients.User targets all connections associated with a user's login name/claims.

questions.question: How do you target only the client who called the method?
questions.answer: Use the Clients.Caller property inside the Hub method.

topics.title: Group Management
topics.html:
Group Management

Course: SignalR

Add and remove connection IDs dynamically into named logical groups to filter messages.

💡 Key Concepts

  • Groups.AddToGroupAsync: Adds a connection ID to a specific named group.
  • Groups.RemoveFromGroupAsync: Removes a connection ID from a group.
  • No persisting: Group memberships are not stored. If a connection drops, membership is lost.

💻 Practical Code Example

C# / CODE BLOCK
public async Task JoinRoom(string roomName) {
    await Groups.AddToGroupAsync(Context.ConnectionId, roomName);
}

⚠️ Common Pitfalls & Mistakes

Assuming group members persist during reconnections. When a client reconnects, you must re-add them to their groups.

questions.question: Are SignalR groups stored in a database?
questions.answer: No, group memberships are managed in-memory by default. You must re-assign groups upon client reconnection.

questions.question: Can you list all members of a group in SignalR?
questions.answer: No, there is no built-in API to list members for security and scalability reasons. You must track memberships in your own service.

topics.title: Client-Side Integration (React Setup)
topics.html:
Client-Side Integration (React Setup)

Course: SignalR

Establish and manage connections in a React frontend using the @microsoft/signalr npm library.

💡 Key Concepts

  • HubConnectionBuilder: Configure and initialize the backend endpoint connection.
  • connection.on: Register listener handlers to receive server commands.
  • withAutomaticReconnect: Ensures the client tries to reconnect if the connection drops.

💻 Practical Code Example

C# / CODE BLOCK
import { HubConnectionBuilder } from "@microsoft/signalr";

const conn = new HubConnectionBuilder()
    .withUrl("https://localhost:5001/chat")
    .withAutomaticReconnect()
    .build();
await conn.start();

⚠️ Common Pitfalls & Mistakes

Calling connection.start() on every React component re-render, creating duplicate connections and slowing the browser.

questions.question: How do you register message listeners in the JS client?
questions.answer: Use connection.on("MethodName", (args) => { ... }) after building the connection.

questions.question: What does withAutomaticReconnect() do?
questions.answer: It automatically attempts to reconnect using standard delay intervals if the connection drops.

topics.title: Authentication & Security in SignalR
topics.html:
Authentication & Security in SignalR

Course: SignalR

Secure SignalR hubs using JWT authorization headers or cookies, and validate connection access.

💡 Key Concepts

  • Authorize Attribute: Enforcing login rules on hubs ([Authorize]).
  • JWT Query String: Browsers do not support headers in WebSockets, so tokens must pass in query strings.
  • CORS rules: Configuring allowed client origins in the backend API.

💻 Practical Code Example

C# / CODE BLOCK
[Authorize]
public class SecureHub : Hub {
    // Only authenticated users can call methods
}

⚠️ Common Pitfalls & Mistakes

Forgetting to register the query string token reader in the JWT authentication options in Program.cs.

questions.question: How do you pass a JWT token to a WebSocket connection?
questions.answer: Configure the client to pass the token as an access token in the query string, and configure the server to read it from the query string.

questions.question: Can you authorize individual methods on a Hub?
questions.answer: Yes, by applying the [Authorize] attribute to specific hub methods.

topics.title: Multi-Server Scaling & Backplanes (Redis, Azure)
topics.html:
Multi-Server Scaling & Backplanes (Redis, Azure)

Course: SignalR

Scale SignalR apps across multiple servers using a Redis backplane or Azure SignalR Service.

💡 Key Concepts

  • Scaleout challenge: Clients on server A will not receive messages sent by clients on server B.
  • Redis Backplane: Publishes messages across all app servers using Redis.
  • Azure SignalR Service: Offloads connection management to a managed service.

💻 Practical Code Example

C# / CODE BLOCK
// In Program.cs (Redis scaleout)
builder.Services.AddSignalR()
    .AddStackExchangeRedis("localhost:6379");

⚠️ Common Pitfalls & Mistakes

Not configuring sticky sessions in load balancers when using multiple servers without a backplane.

questions.question: Why is a Backplane needed for multiple servers?
questions.answer: To broadcast messages sent to one server across all servers, ensuring all connected clients receive it.

questions.question: What is Azure SignalR Service?
questions.answer: A fully managed service that handles connection scale-out, offloading connection management from your app servers.

topics.title: Resilience, Handshakes & Reconnection
topics.html:
Resilience, Handshakes & Reconnection

Course: SignalR

Handle handshakes and reconnection states to ensure reliable communication.

💡 Key Concepts

  • Connection Handshake: The initial request to negotiate protocols and serialization format.
  • Automatic Reconnection: Attempts to reconnect immediately, and then at increasing intervals.
  • Ping Messages: Periodic messages exchanged between client and server to keep the connection alive.

💻 Practical Code Example

C# / CODE BLOCK
connection.onreconnected(connectionId => {
    console.log("Connection restored. New ID: " + connectionId);
});

⚠️ Common Pitfalls & Mistakes

Not handling onreconnecting and onreconnected events in the UI, leaving the user unaware of connection drops.

questions.question: What happens during a SignalR handshake?
questions.answer: The client and server exchange a negotiation request to choose the transport protocol and formatting (JSON/MessagePack).

questions.question: How do you detect when a client is trying to reconnect?
questions.answer: By subscribing to the connection.onreconnecting event handler in the client.

topics.title: Streaming (Server & Client)
topics.html:
Streaming (Server & Client)

Course: SignalR

Stream data from the server to the client (or client to server) to handle large data sets in real-time.

💡 Key Concepts

  • Server-to-Client Streaming: The server sends data chunks sequentially using IAsyncEnumerable.
  • Client-to-Server Streaming: The client streams chunks to the server using ChannelReader.
  • Performance: Saves memory by avoiding loading large datasets into a single message.

💻 Practical Code Example

C# / CODE BLOCK
public async IAsyncEnumerable<int> Counter(int count) {
    for (int i = 0; i < count; i++) {
        await Task.Delay(1000);
        yield return i; // Streams numbers one by one
    }
}

⚠️ Common Pitfalls & Mistakes

Loading an entire collection in memory before yielding it in a streaming method, which defeats the purpose of streaming.

questions.question: What C# return type enables server-to-client streaming?
questions.answer: IAsyncEnumerable<T> or ChannelReader<T>.

questions.question: When should you use streaming in SignalR?
questions.answer: When transferring large data sets (like file chunks or live reports) that should be rendered incrementally.

topics.title: Monitoring, Hub Filters & Diagnostics
topics.html:
Monitoring, Hub Filters & Diagnostics

Course: SignalR

Monitor connection metrics and log hub execution times using Hub Filters.

💡 Key Concepts

  • Hub Filters: Interceptors that run before or after hub method execution.
  • Logging: Configure SignalR log levels in appsettings.json.
  • Performance metrics: Tracking active connections, request counts, and execution latency.

💻 Practical Code Example

C# / CODE BLOCK
public class LogFilter : IHubFilter {
    public async ValueTask<object> InvokeMethodAsync(
        HubInvocationContext context, Func<HubInvocationContext, ValueTask<object>> next) {
        Console.WriteLine($"Calling hub method: {context.HubMethodName}");
        return await next(context);
    }
}

⚠️ Common Pitfalls & Mistakes

Adding blocking operations inside Hub Filters, which slows down all connection communication.

questions.question: What is a Hub Filter?
questions.answer: An interceptor that runs before and after a Hub method is called, allowing you to log or validate requests.

questions.question: How do you monitor connection count in SignalR?
questions.answer: By tracking connection events in OnConnectedAsync and OnDisconnectedAsync, or using performance counters.

topics.title: Intro to C# & .NET Runtime
topics.html:
Intro to C# & .NET Runtime

Course: C# Programming

C# is a modern, type-safe, object-oriented programming language that compiles to Intermediate Language (IL). The .NET Runtime (CLR) compiles this IL into native machine code and manages execution.

💡 Key Concepts

  • Common Language Runtime (CLR): The engine that runs managed code, handling memory, garbage collection, and type safety.
  • Intermediate Language (IL): C# source code is compiled into IL, which is CPU-independent bytecode.
  • Common Type System (CTS): Defines how types are declared, used, and managed in the .NET runtime to allow cross-language integration.

💻 Practical Code Example

C# / CODE BLOCK
using System;
class Program {
    static void Main() {
        Console.WriteLine("C# Code running under Common Language Runtime (CLR)!");
    }
}

⚠️ Common Pitfalls & Mistakes

Confusing C# language features (like switch expressions) with .NET runtime capabilities. Runtimes execute assembly binaries, while C# compilers translate syntax.

questions.question: What is the CLR in .NET?
questions.answer: The Common Language Runtime is the execution engine that loads, validates, compiles (via JIT), and manages memory for .NET assemblies.

questions.question: What is JIT compilation?
questions.answer: Just-In-Time compilation converts IL (Intermediate Language) bytecode into native machine-readable instructions at runtime.

topics.title: Variables, Data Types & Nullables
topics.html:
Variables, Data Types & Nullables

Course: C# Programming

Variables hold values of specific types. Nullable types allow value types (like int, bool) to be assigned a value of null, which is useful when working with databases.

💡 Key Concepts

  • Value Types: Primitives (int, double) and structs stored on the stack containing actual data.
  • Nullable Types (T?): Wrappers that allow assigning null to value types using Nullable.
  • Null Coalescing (??): Operator used to define a default value if a variable evaluates to null.

💻 Practical Code Example

C# / CODE BLOCK
int? count = null;
int actualCount = count ?? 0; // fallback to 0
Console.WriteLine($"Count: {actualCount}");

⚠️ Common Pitfalls & Mistakes

Accessing a nullable variable's Value property directly (e.g. nullable.Value) when it is null. This throws an InvalidOperationException. Always check HasValue first or use HasValue/Value pattern.

questions.question: What are Nullable Types in C#?
questions.answer: Nullable types are instances of System.Nullable<T> struct, allowing value types to represent an undefined or null state.

questions.question: What is the difference between null-coalescing (??) and null-conditional (?.) operators?
questions.answer: ?? returns the right operand if the left is null, while ?. short-circuits member access, returning null if the parent reference is null.

topics.title: Value Types vs Reference Types
topics.html:
Value Types vs Reference Types

Course: C# Programming

C# partitions types into Value Types (stored on the Stack, copied by value) and Reference Types (stored on the Heap, copied by reference pointer).

💡 Key Concepts

  • Stack Memory: Fast, automatic, and small memory used for local execution frames and value types.
  • Heap Memory: Large, managed storage where objects (reference types) are allocated and reclaimed by Garbage Collection.
  • Boxing & Unboxing: The CPU overhead of wrapping value types into heap-allocated object wrappers.

💻 Practical Code Example

C# / CODE BLOCK
struct MyStruct { public int X; } // Value type
class MyClass { public int X; } // Reference type

MyStruct s1 = new MyStruct() { X = 5 };
MyStruct s2 = s1; s2.X = 10; // s1.X remains 5

MyClass c1 = new MyClass() { X = 5 };
MyClass c2 = c1; c2.X = 10; // c1.X changes to 10!

⚠️ Common Pitfalls & Mistakes

Implicit boxing of value types inside collections (e.g. ArrayList), which creates unnecessary heap allocations and triggers heavy garbage collections.

questions.question: What is boxing and unboxing?
questions.answer: Boxing is converting a value type to a reference type (heap allocation). Unboxing is casting it back (stack conversion).

questions.question: Are structs always allocated on the Stack?
questions.answer: No, structs are stored inline within their container. If a struct is a field inside a class, it is stored on the heap as part of that class instance.

topics.title: Control Flow & Loops
topics.html:
Control Flow & Loops

Course: C# Programming

Control flow manages conditional execution and iteration using blocks like if-else, switch, for, foreach, and while.

💡 Key Concepts

  • Conditional statements: Directing path execution using if-else structures or pattern-matching switch blocks.
  • Foreach Iteration: Looping over collections that implement the IEnumerable interface.
  • Break & Continue: Controlling loop exits or skipping to the next loop cycle.

💻 Practical Code Example

C# / CODE BLOCK
var names = new List<string> { "Alice", "Bob", "Charlie" };
foreach (var name in names) {
    if (name.StartsWith("B")) continue; // skip Bob
    Console.WriteLine(name);
}

⚠️ Common Pitfalls & Mistakes

Modifying a collection inside a foreach loop. This invalidates the collection's enumerator, causing an InvalidOperationException at runtime.

questions.question: Why does modifying a collection during foreach throw an error?
questions.answer: The IEnumerator tracks state changes. If you call Add or Remove, the collection version changes, and the iterator throws InvalidOperationException to protect integrity.

questions.question: When is a while loop preferred over a for loop?
questions.answer: When the number of iterations is not known in advance and depends on a condition being met during execution.

topics.title: Classes, Structs, and Records
topics.html:
Classes, Structs, and Records

Course: C# Programming

C# offers three main ways to define data blueprints. Classes support full inheritance, Structs are lightweight value types, and Records provide value-based equality out-of-the-box (ideal for immutable data models).

💡 Key Concepts

  • Classes: Mutable reference types that support OOP hierarchies.
  • Structs: Lightweight value types that avoid heap allocation overhead.
  • Records: Types with built-in value-equality, formatting, and the "with" expression for non-destructive mutation.

💻 Practical Code Example

C# / CODE BLOCK
public record User(string Name, string Role); // Immutable Record
var u1 = new User("Ashutosh", "Admin");
var u2 = u1 with { Role = "User" }; // Non-destructive mutation

⚠️ Common Pitfalls & Mistakes

Declaring large structs (more than 16 bytes). Because structs are value types, they are copied by copying all data bytes. Passing large structs around causes high memory copy overhead.

questions.question: What is a Record in C#?
questions.answer: A Record is a class or struct that provides built-in value equality, standard string formatting, and support for non-destructive mutations via with expressions.

questions.question: When should you use a struct over a class?
questions.answer: Use structs for small, short-lived, immutable data objects (like points or coordinates) that are less than 16 bytes.

topics.title: Properties & Indexers
topics.html:
Properties & Indexers

Course: C# Programming

Properties expose private variables safely, while indexers allow objects to be queried using bracket notation, mimicking array indices.

💡 Key Concepts

  • Auto-Implemented Properties: Direct properties where the compiler manages the backing private variable.
  • Expression-Bodied Members: Compact property definitions using lambda expressions.
  • Indexers: Declared using the "this" keyword, indexers allow custom array-like routing lookup.

💻 Practical Code Example

C# / CODE BLOCK
public class CourseCatalog {
    private string[] courses = { "C#", "SQL", "Docker" };
    public string this[int index] { // Indexer
        get => courses[index];
        set => courses[index] = value;
    }
}

⚠️ Common Pitfalls & Mistakes

Creating infinite recursion loops in properties by returning the property itself instead of the backing field inside the custom get accessor.

questions.question: What is an Indexer in C#?
questions.answer: An indexer is a member that enables instances of a class or struct to be indexed in the same way as arrays using brackets.

questions.question: What is the init keyword in C# properties?
questions.answer: The init keyword restricts property assignment to object initialization blocks, enforcing immutability thereafter.

topics.title: OOP Principles in C#
topics.html:
OOP Principles in C#

Course: C# Programming
