questions.answer: A compilation behavior where SQL Server compiles a procedure plan using the parameters passed on the first run, which can be inefficient for other parameter values.

topics.title: Views & Triggers
topics.html:
Views & Triggers

Course: SQL Server

Create virtual tables using Views, and intercept database actions (Insert, Update, Delete) using Triggers.

💡 Key Concepts

  • View: A virtual table based on a SELECT query. Simplifies security and complex queries.
  • DML Triggers: Code executed automatically when data in a table is modified.
  • Inserted & Deleted Tables: Temporary tables accessible inside triggers containing row state modifications.

💻 Practical Code Example

C# / CODE BLOCK
CREATE VIEW ActiveEmployees AS
SELECT Id, Name FROM Employees WHERE IsActive = 1;

⚠️ Common Pitfalls & Mistakes

Overusing Triggers to manage business logic, which makes debugging extremely difficult because code runs invisibly.

questions.question: What are the Inserted and Deleted tables in triggers?
questions.answer: Temporary, memory-resident tables containing the state of rows before and after the modification.

questions.question: Does a view store data physically?
questions.answer: No, standard views are virtual tables. Indexed views (materialized views), however, do store data physically on disk.

topics.title: ACID Properties & Transactions
topics.html:
ACID Properties & Transactions

Course: SQL Server

Ensure database integrity using transactions that satisfy ACID properties: Atomicity, Consistency, Isolation, and Durability.

💡 Key Concepts

  • Atomicity: Ensures all database actions in a transaction succeed, or all roll back (All-or-Nothing).
  • Consistency: Guarantees the database transitions from one valid state to another.
  • Isolation / Durability: Isolation keeps concurrent transactions separate. Durability ensures committed changes survive crashes.

💻 Practical Code Example

C# / CODE BLOCK
BEGIN TRANSACTION;
BEGIN TRY
    UPDATE Accounts SET Balance -= 100 WHERE Id = 1;
    UPDATE Accounts SET Balance += 100 WHERE Id = 2;
    COMMIT TRANSACTION;
END TRY
BEGIN CATCH
    ROLLBACK TRANSACTION;
END CATCH;

⚠️ Common Pitfalls & Mistakes

Leaving transactions open by forgetting COMMIT or ROLLBACK, which blocks locks and causes database freezes.

questions.question: What does ACID stand for?
questions.answer: Atomicity, Consistency, Isolation, and Durability, the core principles of reliable database transactions.

questions.question: What happens if a SQL query fails inside a BEGIN TRANSACTION block without error handling?
questions.answer: The transaction remains open and lock resources stay blocked until the connection is closed or rolled back.

topics.title: Transaction Isolation Levels
topics.html:
Transaction Isolation Levels

Course: SQL Server

Control database locks behavior and prevent anomalies like Dirty Reads, Non-Repeatable Reads, and Phantom Reads.

💡 Key Concepts

  • Read Uncommitted: Allows reading uncommitted data, causing Dirty Reads. Low lock overhead.
  • Read Committed: Default level. Prevents dirty reads by holding shared locks until reads finish.
  • Serializable: Highest isolation. Places range locks to prevent phantom reads.

💻 Practical Code Example

C# / CODE BLOCK
SET TRANSACTION ISOLATION LEVEL SNAPSHOT;
BEGIN TRANSACTION;
SELECT * FROM Products;
COMMIT TRANSACTION;

⚠️ Common Pitfalls & Mistakes

Setting isolation level to Serializable unnecessarily, which blocks concurrent queries and slows down execution.

questions.question: What is a dirty read?
questions.answer: Reading data that has been modified by an active transaction but has not yet been committed.

questions.question: How does Snapshot isolation prevent locking readers?
questions.answer: It uses row versioning in tempdb to show readers the data state at the start of the transaction, avoiding shared locks.

topics.title: Indexing Strategies & Query Optimization
topics.html:
Indexing Strategies & Query Optimization

Course: SQL Server

Optimize database tables using Clustered and Non-Clustered indexes, and analyze execution plans.

💡 Key Concepts

  • Clustered Index: Re-orders table data physically on disk. Only 1 per table.
  • Non-Clustered Index: A separate search index pointing to row IDs. Multiple allowed.
  • Covering Index: Adding INCLUDE columns to indexes so queries resolve entirely within the index.

💻 Practical Code Example

C# / CODE BLOCK
CREATE CLUSTERED INDEX IX_Employees_Id ON Employees(Id);
CREATE NONCLUSTERED INDEX IX_Employees_Email ON Employees(Email) INCLUDE(Name);

⚠️ Common Pitfalls & Mistakes

Adding indexes to every column, which slows down INSERT, UPDATE, and DELETE queries because all indexes must be rebuilt.

questions.question: What is a covering index?
questions.answer: An index that contains all the columns referenced by a query, allowing results to resolve without table lookups.

questions.question: What is the difference between an Index Scan and an Index Seek?
questions.answer: A scan searches the entire index tree (slow). A seek navigates directly to matching rows using search keys (fast).

topics.title: Database Normalization
topics.html:
Database Normalization

Course: SQL Server

Minimize data redundancy and prevent anomalies by normalizing tables into 1NF, 2NF, 3NF, and BCNF.

💡 Key Concepts

  • 1NF (First Normal Form): Atomic columns and unique rows. No repeating groups.
  • 2NF (Second Normal Form): Meets 1NF. Removes partial dependencies (all columns depend on the entire primary key).
  • 3NF (Third Normal Form): Meets 2NF. Removes transitive dependencies (non-key columns depend only on the primary key).

💻 Practical Code Example

C# / CODE BLOCK
// 3NF Rule: ZipCode table should hold City/State columns,
// and Customers table should only store ZipCodeId.

⚠️ Common Pitfalls & Mistakes

Over-normalizing simple databases, which requires joining too many tables for basic queries and slows down performance.

questions.question: What is transitive dependency in 3NF?
questions.answer: When a non-key column depends on another non-key column, rather than directly on the primary key.

questions.question: When is denormalization acceptable?
questions.answer: In read-heavy reporting systems (Data Warehouses) to reduce JOIN complexity and speed up reads.

topics.title: SQL Server Security Policies
topics.html:
SQL Server Security Policies

Course: SQL Server

Secure database instances using logins, users, schemas, and Row-Level Security (RLS).

💡 Key Concepts

  • Logins vs Users: Logins grant server connection access. Users grant access to specific databases.
  • Row-Level Security (RLS): Filters query rows automatically based on user roles and security predicates.
  • SQL Injection Prevention: Always use parameterized queries, never concatenate SQL strings.

💻 Practical Code Example

C# / CODE BLOCK
CREATE SECURITY POLICY SalesFilter
ADD FILTRATION PREDICATE dbo.fn_securitypredicate(SalesPersonId)
ON dbo.Orders;

⚠️ Common Pitfalls & Mistakes

Using the "sa" (system administrator) account for application connections, exposing full database access.

questions.question: What is the difference between a Login and a User?
questions.answer: A Login is for server authentication. A User is database-specific, mapping a login to table access.

questions.question: How do parameterized queries prevent SQL injection?
questions.answer: By treating inputs strictly as literal values rather than executable SQL commands.

topics.title: Disaster Recovery (Backup & Restore)
topics.html:
Disaster Recovery (Backup & Restore)

Course: SQL Server

Plan database recovery strategies using Full, Differential, and Transaction Log backups.

💡 Key Concepts

  • Backup Types: Full (entire DB), Differential (changes since last Full), Log (changes since last Log backup).
  • Recovery Models: Simple (no log backups, auto-truncates), Full (retains transaction logs, allows point-in-time recovery).
  • Point-In-Time Restore: Restoring a database to a specific second before a corruption event.

💻 Practical Code Example

C# / CODE BLOCK
BACKUP DATABASE TutorialDb TO DISK = 'D:\Backup\TutorialDb.bak';
BACKUP LOG TutorialDb TO DISK = 'D:\Backup\TutorialDb_Log.trn';

⚠️ Common Pitfalls & Mistakes

Running database recovery in Full Recovery Model without setting up Transaction Log backups, causing transaction log files (.ldf) to grow until the disk is full.

questions.question: Why does the transaction log grow continuously in Full Recovery Model?
questions.answer: Because SQL Server keeps the log until a Transaction Log backup is run to truncate committed logs.

questions.question: What is a differential backup?
questions.answer: A backup that contains all changes made to the database since the last full database backup.
